subject: Insurance
title: The Triangle Shirtwaist Fire
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Triangle Shirtwaist Fire usable.

hook.text: In 1911, 146 workers died in a New York garment factory fire. Doors were locked.

buildup.text: The Triangle Shirtwaist Company packed 600 workers into cramped upper floors. Fire escapes were inadequate.

discovery.text: The owners collected $60,000 more in insurance than their losses.

twist.text: Public outrage forced New York to pass 36 workplace safety laws.

climax.text: Triangle Shirtwaist transformed American labor law.

punchline.text: 146 dead, owners profited. One factory fire created US workplace safety laws.

quiz.question: What major change did the Triangle Shirtwaist fire cause?
options: Mandatory workplace safety laws and workers' compensation
